## Installation

The current version of the package allows to follow described data processing
protocols, estimate swept area indices and plot results.

To get started with *DATRASextra*, install and load the package:

```{r, eval = FALSE, echo = TRUE, fig.alt = ""}

## Install the package
remotes::install_github("tokami/DATRASextra")

## Load the package into R
library(DATRASextra)
```

## Basic use

DATRASextra makes it easy to download survey data from ICES DATRAS database:

```{r, eval = FALSE, echo = TRUE, fig.alt = ""}
survey <- "SNS"
tmp <- tempdir()
downloadDATRAS(surveys = survey, years = 2023, dir = tmp)
```

This mainly uses the functionality of the DATRAS R package but allows a bit more
flexibility, like specifying the path were the data should be installed to.

Next, the data can be read into R with:

```{r, eval = FALSE, echo = TRUE, fig.alt = ""}
surv0 <- readDATRAS(file.path(tmp, survey))
```

Now, you can process, subset, modify and analyse the data:

```{r, eval = FALSE, echo = TRUE, fig.alt = ""}
surv <- clean(surv0)

plot(surv)
```



## Advanced use

Demo of one advanced use case.

```{r, eval = FALSE, echo = TRUE, fig.alt = ""}
surv <- clean(surv0)

plot(surv)
```

More advanced options are shown in the vignettes.
